newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Siemens Nixdorf targets $1 bln Asian sales by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Siemens Nixdorf targets $1 bln Asian sales by 2000.

text.p: German computer giant Siemens Nixdorf Informationssysteme AG aims to more than triple its Asia-Pacific sales to US$1 billion by the year 2000, executive vice president Axel Hass said on Wednesday.
Hass told Reuters in an interview the company, part of German's second largest industrial group, Siemens AG, was well on the way to achieving this goal.
He said he was confident the company would increase its Asian sales by 40 to 50 percent a year over the next four years.
"We are the fastest growing IT (information technology) company in Asia," he said.
"We have a vision -- the number one European IT company aims to become a US$1 billion company within the Asia-Pacific by the year 2000," he said.
Hass said most Asian growth would come in China, Indonesia, Malaysia and India and he expected around 30 percent of Asia-Pacific sales in 2000, or around US$300 million, to come from China alone.
"These are countries with a high population and these are the big growth areas, as well as Australia of course," he said.

Siemens Nixdorf had a total Asia-Pacific turnover of just US$170 million in its last financial year to September 30, 1995 with external turnover (sales to non-Siemens customers) amounting to some US$90 million.
"This year we will expect to double the (external sales) figure," he said.
He said the group projected a 65 percent rise in total Asia-Pacific sales in the year to September 30, 1996, from around US$170 million in 1994/95.
Hass said the company currently had a "tiny" market share in the Asia-Pacific region.
Its share of the lucrative automated teller machines (ATM) market and "point-of-sale" market for direct debit machines, for example, was only around one percent, he said.
"So there is plenty of scope for growth," he said. "In four or five years our share could be 20 or 30 percent."
Within Siemens Nixdorf, the Asia-Pacific region only accounted for around 2.5 or 3.0 percent of total worldwide turnover, but this would rise quickly, he said.

"What we want to reach, as a first step, is one third of total business from the United States and Asia-Pacific over the next few years...eventually Asia-Pacific should be one third of business on its own," he said.

Hass said the fastest growing part of Siemens Nixdorf business was in "integrated business solutions" where Siemens Nixdorf was invited in by a company to organise its information technology and production systems in the most efficient manner.

"For example, a customer is building a new factory and wants to solve a number of problems: how the material flows through his company, where does he buy, how he arranges the warehouse, how end-products get out into the market," he said.
"He is looking for an IT supplier who can help him solve the problem. We do it."
"This is 30 percent of our business now in Asia-Pacific and it is growing fast," he said.
